subject: Orchard Health POC: hands-on kickoff & capacity planning
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Kathy Lee <kathy.lee@orchard.ai>, Orchard DevOps <devops@orchard.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Feb 2027 16:18:00 -0800
Subject: Orchard Health — POC hands-on kickoff & capacity planning

Hi Kathy —

Thanks again for agreeing to run a hands-on POC with Redwood. To make the working session productive, we'd like to schedule two blocks: a 90-minute kickoff/hands-on where we walk through prompt patterns, routing rules, and run a short load test; and a follow-up 60-minute capacity planning session (Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs, rate limit/quota needs, token budgeting).

Suggested windows next week (PST):
- Tues 2027-02-16: 10:00–11:30 or 15:00–16:30
- Wed 2027-02-17: 09:30–11:00 or 14:00–15:30

Agenda (short):
- Intros & objectives (10m)
- Prompt review + demo prompts (25m)
- Routing and fallback plans (20m)
- Quick load run (20m)
- Next steps & capacity follow-up (15m)

I've attached a preliminary agenda and a capacity worksheet to help you fill in current token volumes and concurrency targets. Can you confirm which windows work and whether we should invite anyone from infra to the capacity session?

Thanks — looking forward.

Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com
(415) 555-0134

Attachments: Orchard_POC_Agenda_v1.pdf (pdf), POC_capacity_plan.xlsx (xlsx)

Subject: Re: Orchard Health — POC hands-on kickoff & capacity planning

Hi Mina —

Thanks — this looks great. We can do the kickoff on Tue 2027-02-16 at 15:00 PST. For the capacity session, our infra lead (cc'ed DevOps) prefers Wed 2027-02-17 morning, but they asked whether we can move the final 60-minute session to Thu 2027-02-18 at 10:00 so they have time to pull token aggregates and concurrency targets.

Quick notes:
- We usually test at 95th percentile loads; on a short run we'll target 200 concurrent sessions, ~1.2M tokens/day equivalent.
- Please include a short section on how Redwood handles KV-cache warmup and cold-start token costs — that's a hard ask for our SREs.

Kathy
Kathy Lee
Head of Product, Orchard Health
kathy.lee@orchard.ai

Looping everyone in — great availability from Kathy. Marcus, can you own the short load test orchestration? Priyom, please prepare two routing scenarios (single-model hosted vs quantized dedicated) we can show tradeoffs for latency and token cost.

Also, Kathy requested KV-cache cold-start behavior. Marcus — include a 5-slide quick explainer and a 5–10 minute demo of warm vs cold inference in the kickoff. Attachments: prompt-workshop-notes.md (I'll drop a starter prompt set).

Next action: Marcus to confirm readiness + any infra hooks needed by Friday EOD. Mina — I'll handle the calendar invites once slots are final.

Aditya Rao

Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 14:47:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Orchard Health — POC hands-on kickoff & capacity planning

Kathy / team —

I can run the load portion and will bring two pre-provisioned environments: one hosted baseline and one dedicated (4xA10G equiv) for a short 10-minute ramp to ~200 concurrent sessions. I'll include telemetry so we can show per-token latency and cost delta.

For KV-cache: we'll run a short cold-start (empty KV) vs warmed (30s of synthetic prefixes) to show the hit. If you can share sample prompt prefixes ahead of time that will help — I've attached prompt-workshop-notes.md with a starter set; feel free to replace placeholders.

Blocked items for the capacity meeting:
- Orchard to provide 7-day token histogram or an estimate (peak 95th percentile)
- Confirmation on whether Dedicated GPUs are available for a short trial (we can request quota bump if needed)

I'll reserve a sandbox project and will need an infra contact to open ports for the short test harness (we'll provide an IP list).

Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
